findings.change: In U-required, before the first mapping lands, leave selectors out of scopeDecision.groupIDs, or treat a path covered only by a selector like a template-covered path, and refuse selectors in RunNamedGroups as it refuses templates.
findings.claim: The lane's scoped proof can pick a selector group (one that names required test files and is never run as itself) as a group to run. The trigger is a changed path that a selector's inputs cover while no Go code unit changes. RunNamedGroups does not refuse selectors, so that scoped proof would stop with 'not run' instead of running.
findings.evidence: testpolicy.Affected (internal/testpolicy/affected.go:46-57) adds every group whose inputs cover a path, selectors included. scopeDecision.groupIDs (internal/landing/plain/scope.go:301-307) turns those into LANDING_PROOF_GROUPS (prove.go:1275). repoproof (internal/repoproof/full.go:153) passes them to proofrun.RunNamedGroups, whose only refusal is for packageSelection (internal/proofrun/groups.go:53-56). The run then fails closed, because GoTests errors on an empty test list (contract.go:696-697). It cannot be reached in this unit: testing.json has no selectors, and the brief puts mappings in the next unit (U-required). Not material: the slice works and is safe without the fix, and the failure is closed, not a false green.
findings.relation: goal intent: every reader of the test contract understands a selector group before any mapping uses one
